extracted.intended_audience: journalists and defense/public-relations officials (and general readers interested in Defense Dept. information policy)
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting on a newly issued Defense Department directive governing release of information, speeches and articles by military personnel, and related public-relations staffing/organization decisions; includes reactions and examples of operational effects (delays, channeling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive-contribution test for released information
rubrics_metrics.description: Released information should 'constitute a constructive contribution to the primary mission of the Department of Defense.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarification from C. Herschel Schooley: this wording 'did not mean that only favorable information would be issued.' It could include news that might be critical but which, in its application, 'could result in correcting faults of the department or armed forces.' (This is the stated substantive standard for deciding what Defense Dept. information to release.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission/approval/channeling requirement for military public statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Speeches and articles written by military personnel for publication, and other public information items, must be submitted and go through channels and receive covering memoranda/clearance before release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in reporting: a mimeographed obituary sketch of a marine officer was received by a reporter only after it 'had gone through “channels” and been in a covering memorandum.' A routine request for information on a collision took almost 12 hours for a statement to come. Public-relations officials said they 'needed clarification of the order.' The directive was prepared by legal experts and presented to Public Information officials after completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational policy consideration: civilianizing public information leadership and staff reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: A memorandum advised the Army, Navy and Air Force secretaries to 'study the possibility of appointing civilians to replace the military chiefs of public information in their departments and to plan for a reduction in public relations staffs ranging from one-third to ...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an administrative/organizational standard or recommendation included with the directive — it signals an evaluative criterion for staffing structure (civilian vs. military leadership) and for target reductions in PR personnel. Public-relations officials were reported to be seeking clarification on this point as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-pattern / caution: literal strict obedience may impede routine information flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Officials and aides feared that 'officials of the armed services, resentful over the order, were carrying things to extremes by obeying it to the letter even in routine matters.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences cited: routine questions became entangled with interpretations of the order (prompt answers withheld), and over-compliance led to delays (e.g., 12-hour delay on collision statement). This functions as a practical warning about implementing the directive too rigidly and identifies timeliness/operational impact as an implicit evaluative consideration.
